decisions.reason: SOL keeps the unavoidable difference in their natures in natural English.
SOL folds the trained-beast description into the next sentence without dropping the sense.
SOL preserves both the predator’s strength and the hunting dog’s loyalty while avoiding repetition.
“Spring into action” naturally preserves his immediate, unhesitating response.
“Had barely sounded when” preserves the signal’s immediacy and the swift blade swing.
The Korean specifically says Jamukha’s foot shoots forward; SOL changes the action to his whole body shooting forward.
SOL keeps the figure’s sudden blur; “in an instant” is redundant with the source’s momentary timing.
SOL preserves the technique and fleeting timing without the awkward “unleashed” construction.
“Raced toward” keeps the direction and adds natural momentum to the charge.
SOL preserves the near-certainty in Jamukha’s movements and the denial that it is baseless.
“Speed above all else” preserves his pursuit of extreme speed in more natural phrasing.
SOL retains the gap accumulated over the long years; the recast is idiomatic.
SOL preserves the caterpillar image and the newly changed view of the world.
“Drawn his power beyond its limits” keeps the pill’s effect and the power still seething within him.
“Awakened” and “bearing down” naturally convey the opened sixth sense and the incoming flame.
“Picked up speed” preserves his acceleration in natural English.
SOL keeps the leap over the dust and the image of his wind-erasing rush.
SOL preserves that his resolve is not the loyalty of a dog to its master.
“Come together” preserves how the other man’s strength and Jamukha’s ambitions brought about his submission.

SOL preserves the slash bringing him closer to the previously stated ambition.
SOL preserves Jeok Cheongang’s apparent inability to react and his continued fight with the Demon Lord.
SOL keeps Jamukha’s certainty; the referent remains clear from the preceding lines.

SOL keeps the backward bend and the blade’s deflection while trimming redundant wording.
SOL preserves his realization and its cause without the unnecessary “finally.”

SOL preserves the emphatic certainty in natural English.
SOL keeps the contrast from knowing to trusting; the expanded contraction does not alter the beat.
SOL preserves the quiet voice reaching him as he clenches his teeth.
SOL keeps the Force’s renewed surge; “even” is not needed to preserve the comparison.
SOL preserves that the technique was perfected through pursuit of extreme speed.

SOL preserves the comparison between Jamukha’s strength and speed and Jin Taekyung’s enlightenment and rewards.
SOL retains the blaze, Jamukha’s lurch, and the heat ravaging his acupoints.
SOL preserves the fading vision and the blood rising from his dantian.

“Kept welling up” preserves the pill’s continuously replenishing power.
SOL preserves the vitality holding him together when his body should already have collapsed.

SOL preserves the sight of Jin Taekyung in pain and Jamukha forcing out his question.
SOL preserves the appearance of the red-tinged armor over skin exposed through his torn clothes.

SOL keeps the five fingers embedded in his flank like a hook and Jin Taekyung’s tired response.
SOL preserves the request to make things easy, the complaint about Jamukha holding on, and the saved technique.

SOL preserves that both the Force and the blade have lost their potency.
SOL preserves the failed strike, regretful scrape across the armor, and the blade slipping away.
SOL keeps the explosion deep inside him without the unnecessary “reverberate.”
SOL preserves the distant, detached sensation and the image of watching from far away.
SOL preserves the blood’s heat and the singular shout attributable to the North Heaven Demon Lord.
SOL keeps his staggering under the force and inability to step back.
SOL preserves the burning pain and the fingers holding him like a hook.

SOL’s fragment continues the preceding sentence and preserves the point at which the pill’s power is spent.
“Ran dry” naturally preserves the sea of power finally becoming exhausted.
“Could no longer feel pain” preserves his realization that the pain had ceased.
“Eyes moved weakly upward” preserves the action without the awkward “rolled.”
SOL preserves the unfinished thought addressing Jin Taekyung.

SOL preserves the wavering heat haze and the lifeless king of the steppe.

SOL preserves the repeated strikes, internal energy, and lips returning from white to red.
SOL retains the sense of spent and worn-away things returning to their original state.
